lesson_title: One Impala to the Whole Planet in Six Zooms
hook_text: Is a dead leaf alive or not? Get it wrong and you lose the mark. Here is the rule, and the six boxes around one impala.
clip_script: One impala in the Kruger. That is an organism. Zoom out: all the impala in that area, one species, one place, one time. Population. Zoom out: every living thing there, lions, grass, thorn trees, dung beetles, bacteria. Community. Now add the sun, the rain, the soil, the air, the heat. Living plus non-living, all mixed together: ecosystem. Zoom out: the whole savanna region with its climate. Biome. One more: every ecosystem on Earth. Biosphere. Six boxes, each inside the next. Inside the ecosystem, two columns. Biotic is anything alive or that was alive, so the dead leaf, the bone, the dung all go there. Abiotic is what was never alive: water, rock, sunlight, temperature. The stage and the actors. The stage decides who acts: rain makes forests, dry makes Karoo. But the actors rebuild the stage: trees make shade, termites turn soil, elephants flatten woodland. Six zooms, two columns, done.
visual_style: A single impala icon with concentric labelled rings expanding outward to a globe; then a two-column board where a dead-leaf icon slides into the biotic column.
mood: Brisk, visual, a little cheeky on the dead leaf.
pacing: Six fast zooms, a pause on the dead leaf, quick two-column finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sort any ecosystem into its two columns.
